sources.notes: Company annual-report archive: Asian financial crisis and weaker U.S. demand left excess stock and discounting in fiscal 1998; revenue growth slowed to 4% and gross margin fell from 40.1% to 36.5%.

Retrospective fiscal 2001 discussion: new demand/supply planning system caused excess stock, shortages and late deliveries; U.S. footwear revenue fell 4.2%, international revenue grew, and net income was $589.7 million. Fiscal 2002 revenue grew 4.3% to $9.89 billion. Scenarios ending before May 2002 use only the report’s 2001 facts.

Only fiscal 2001 facts used: GO.com closure caused $878 million restructuring/impairment charges; ABC had lower ratings and weaker advertising; September 11 closures and reduced travel hurt park attendance. Disney California Adventure opened in fiscal 2001. Does not narrate fiscal 2002 totals after the April/July endpoints.

Annual filing linked from Apple Investor Relations (FilingId=107083): 1997 NeXT acquisition, August 1998 iMac launch, product simplification and $309 million fiscal 1998 profit after a $1.045 billion 1997 loss. Uses figures as reported at the time.

sources.notes: Quarter ended December 29, 2001: net profit $38 million versus a $195 million year-earlier loss; over 125,000 iPods sold in two months and 27 Apple retail stores open by year end.
